correctness.rationale: Schur reduction exhausts all complex two-by-two contractions with eigenvalue r. The positive-semidefinite condition is exactly \(0\le |a|\le1-r^2\); nilpotency gives the exact power-difference and shear singular-value formula. The uniform exponential tail controls the sup over all powers as r tends to one. Mirror comparison excludes the subunit time window, strict monotonicity of the stationarity equation ensures a unique maximizer, and the exact contraction boundary reduces to a unique quartic root. Limiting power localization, the small-c series, and the strong-c golden-ratio slope are derived analytically. The standalone finite checker was executed successfully.

value.rationale: The family of repeated-eigenvalue two-dimensional contractions is the minimal nonnormal setting for the quantitatively important Ritt power-difference estimate. The result is a sharp uniform limiting constant over the full contraction class, with a unique extremal coupling, precise attaining power scale, and an exact parametric profile showing significant nonnormal amplification relative to scalar matrices. These supply natural comparison benchmarks for quantitative Ritt/semigroup regularity rather than arbitrary low-dimensional data.
